IncidentBot: [ALERT] 2456789012 — spike: allocator failures + OOMs observed on cluster gpu-serving-12. 42 OOMs / 5m, automatic paging increased. Pager invoked. https://mon.redwood.example/alerts/2456789012 :rotating_light:
Alex: Ack. I'm the on-call. Pulling logs now. tagging @Priya for runtime triage.
Priya: Joining. saw repeated `CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED` and container restarts. Also some "out of memory" traces from paged-attn allocator during KV warmup.
Ben: Any customer-facing errors yet?
Clara: Support: a handful of prod customers report latency spikes and a few 502s starting ~17:02 UTC. No broad outage but increased error rate for some Dedicated pools.
Sasha: Noting this may affect model large-1 and chat-2 routes that use aggressive KV caching.
Alex: Quick checklist: (1) isolate node(s) (2) reduce incoming traffic to affected pool (3) attempt graceful drain or restart. I'm running `kubectl get pods -n runtime -o wide | grep gpu-serving-12`.
Priya: Running nvidia and allocator diagnostics now. Pasting key snippets:
```
$ kubectl logs runtime-gpu-12 -c runtime --since=10m | tail -n 80
[2026-03-15T17:03:12Z] runtime: paged_attn_alloc: requested 2147483648 bytes, allocated 0
[2026-03-15T17:03:12Z] runtime: kv_cache: slot fragmentation > 0.85, free_slabs=2/128
[2026-03-15T17:03:13Z] cuda: CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED: driver attempted to allocate 2GB
[2026-03-15T17:03:14Z] container: restart backoff: OOM killed
```
Ben: Paging looks like slow creep of fragments — slab free list is nearly drained. Not classic single-flight leak, more fragmentation over time.
Alex: Any quick mitigations before we do rolling restarts?
Priya: Two fast options: 1) force KV eviction to drop fragmented pages `REDWOOD_KV_FORCE_EVICT=1` (hot patch via configmap restart), 2) reduce per-request KV prefetch to avoid large consecutive allocations (config flag `KV_PREFETCH_BYTES=0` temporarily). Both are non-invasive and reversible.
Ben: Also we can flip autoscaling to move traffic off gpu-serving-12 by setting route weight to 0 for that pool (console change). Do that first to stop further pressure.
Alex: I'll start failover: routing change to drain. @Sasha can you coordinate with traffic?
Sasha: Doing it now — moved 90% of traffic off the pool, left ~10% for health checks. Monitor. :white_check_mark:
Priya: After routing change, errors dropped but OOMs persist on that node (residual background). Recommend rolling restart of runtime pods on that node to reclaim memory.
Alex: Ok scheduling `kubectl drain` with pod eviction. Doing one node at a time. I'll annotate runbook.
Priya: While that's happening, applying hot config to trigger KV eviction. Patch applied, rolling restart of runtime daemonset initiated. Patch: `kubectl -n runtime set env configmap/runtime REDWOOD_KV_FORCE_EVICT=1` then `kubectl rollout restart daemonset/runtime`.
deploy-bot: rollout started: daemonset/runtime @ 2456789230 -> 6/6 updated; watch: https://deploy.redwood.example/rollouts/5789
Priya: After first pod restart, observed immediate slab reclamation and a drop in `fragmentation` metric from 0.86 -> 0.42.
Alex: Good. Any persistent CUDA failures in logs post-restart?
Priya: One-off allocation failures during restart ramp, but no sustained CUBLAS errors now.
Ben: Final step: run a compact job: `./tools/kv-compact --target=128` on drained node before bringing it back. This helps coalesce free slabs.
Alex: Doing compact now.
Priya: Also flagged a bug: paged-attn allocator doesn't always return back small fragments into the global free list under heavy interleaved KV activity. I'll open a follow-up PR to tighten freelist accounting and add a conservative periodic compaction.
Sasha: Customer impact update: Clara, can you confirm which customers were affected and whether any retries caused billing anomalies?
Clara: Primary impact: three Dedicated customers on pool gpu-serving-12 saw elevated 5xx for ~8–12 minutes. We've opened CS tickets and notified them. No billing changes detected yet but will monitor.
Ben: Post-mortem actions we should capture: (A) short-term: config flag `REDWOOD_KV_FORCE_EVICT` documented and runbook updated, (B) medium: add automated compaction cron job in runtime, (C) long-term: allocator refactor + better fragmentation telemetry, (D) routing policy tweak to auto-balance if fragmentation metric > 0.8.
Alex: Preparing on-call handoff. Current state: traffic rerouted, daemonset restarted, compact run completed, node reintroduced after health checks. Residual risk: fragmentation may resurface under similar workload.
Alex: Handoff summary for next oncall (Priya covering runtime for 2 hours post-handoff):
- Incident start: 2456789012 UTC — elevated OOMs due to allocator fragmentation.
- Actions taken: traffic reroute, KV eviction hot patch, rolling restart of runtime daemonset on affected node(s), manual kv-compact, customer notifications.
- Current status: All runtime pods stable; allocator fragmentation metric at 0.38; no sustained CUDA errors.
- Follow-ups: Priya to file bug + PR, Ben to add compaction cron, Sasha to review route auto-balance thresholds, Clara to track CS tickets.
Alex: I'm handing off to Priya now. If anything regresses, escalate to Ben and page infra.
Priya: I have the handoff. I'll keep watch for 2 hours and start the allocator PR. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Ben: Will add compaction cron and update runbook this afternoon.
Sasha: I'll draft the incident note for product-impact and customer comms.
Clara: Creating CS follow-ups and logging impacted customers.
IncidentBot: Incident closed (mitigated) at 2456789625 — symptoms reduced below alert thresholds.
Alex: Closing thread. Good job everyone.
Priya: Filed tracker: RT-1429 "paged-attn allocator fragmentation under KV churn". Link: https://tracker.redwood.example/RT-1429
Ben: Postmortem owner: Priya. Deadline: 7 days.
Sasha: I'll coordinate external comms after postmortem review.
Clara: Noted for support debrief at 18:30 UTC.
Alex: End of handoff.
